about.title: Monte Sereno Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Monte Sereno is a small, quiet hillside community, but that doesn't mean falls don't happen — on uneven walkways near Saratoga Los Gatos Road, in parking areas off Winchester Boulevard, or inside local businesses and residences. When a property owner fails to fix a known hazard, like a broken step, wet floor, or poor lighting, someone can get seriously hurt. California law requires you to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the danger and didn't address it. That's why documenting the scene matters. Photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage can make or break a claim, especially since video often gets overwritten within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent local attorney who can evaluate what happened, help preserve evidence, and explain your options under California's premises liability rules. There's no obligation and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Monte Sereno Fall

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timely Evidence
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can move quickly to request incident reports and any available surveillance footage before it's deleted.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability claim in California, though claims against a public entity involve a much shorter window. Talking to someone early helps preserve your options.

items.question: I fell at a small business in Monte Sereno. Is it worth contacting an attorney?
items.answer: It can be, especially since Monte Sereno's local businesses and shared walkways may have limited or short-cycle surveillance systems. An attorney can act quickly to request footage and document the hazard before it's cleaned up or repaired. A free consultation costs you nothing and helps you understand where you stand.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for not noticing the hazard?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your total may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is a fact-specific determination, so it helps to have someone review the details of your fall.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a fall in Monte Sereno?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit in California. If your fall happened on public property, such as a sidewalk maintained by a government entity, that deadline is much shorter. It's best to get guidance as soon as possible so you don't lose your right to pursue a claim.
